M.A.C.A. No. 2184 Of 2014
 Against The Judgment Dated 25.01.2013 In Op(Mv) No.1475 Of
2010 Of Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Kollam

Appellant/Petitioner:
 Subhakumar,
 S/O. Kochunarayanan, Varoor Puthen Veedu, Thazham,
 Chathannoor.

By Advs.
 Sri.Pratheesh.P
 Smt.S.Seetha
Respondents/1St & 3Rd Respondents:
 1 Joy,
 Neethu Bhavan, Adichanalloor, Kollam.
 2 Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.,
 Kollam-691 001.
 By Adv Sri.A.R.George
 This Motor Accident Claims Appeal Having Been Finally Heard
On 04.02.2026, The Court On The Same Day Delivered The Following:
 2026:Ker:11188
M.A.C.A. No. 2184 Of 2014
 2
 J U D G M E N T
This appeal is filed by the claimant in O.P(MV) No. 1475 of 2010 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Kollam, dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

Subhakumar vs Joy on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131604158/
1
The respondents herein were the respondent Nos.1 & 3 respectively before the Tribunal.

2. The case of the claimant is that, on 4.6.2008 at about 9.40 a.m., while the claimant was attempting to get into a mini bus bearing reg. no. KL-01/H 8656, with tools for repairing the bus,
the 2nd respondent moved the bus forward in a rash and negligent manner, due to which the claimant was thrown out of the bus and the back tyre of the bus ran over the hand of the claimant whereby sustaining grievous hurt.
The claimant approached the tribunal claiming a total compensation of 1,50,000/-.
3. The first, second and third respondents were the owner, driver and insurer of the offending mini bus respectively.
Before the Tribunal, the 1st and 2nd respondents remained absent and were set ex-parte.
The third respondent/insurer filed a written statement denying a valid insurance policy and liability.
Exts.A1 to A6 were marked 2026:KER:11188 M.A.C.A. NO. 2184 OF 2014 before the tribunal.

The Tribunal, after analysing the pleadings and materials on record, awarded a sum of 1,34,000/- as compensation under different heads with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till realization against the first respondent being the owner since there was no valid policy for the vehicle; and in default of payment as above, penal interest @ 9% per annum was also awarded.
Dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant had come up in appeal.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for the respondent/insurer.
Though notice was issued to the first respondent/owner, he chose not to appear before this court.

5. The learned counsel for the appellant claims enhancement mainly under the following heads :-
Notional income :-

The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that though an amount of 5,000 was claimed, the Tribunal had taken only an amount of 4,000/-
as the monthly income of the claimant who was a motor mechanic at the time of the accident in 2008.

The learned counsel for the appellant further submitted that, as per the judgment in 2026:KER:11188 M.A.C.A. NO. 2184 OF 2014 Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the income of a coolie for an accident in the year 2008 is fixed at 6,500/- per month and sought for enhancement of fixation of monthly income.

entities.text:
Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Following the judgment in Ramachandrappa (supra) in order to award just compensation, I find it appropriate to refix the monthly income as 6,500/-.
Compensation for pain and sufferings :- The Tribunal has awarded only an amount of 12,000/- under the head pain and sufferings.

Considering the nature of the injuries such as near total amputation of little finger and ring finger sustained by the claimant, I find that a total amount of 30,000/- can be awarded under the said head.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 18,000/- under the afore head.
Compensation for loss of income:-

The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that towards loss of earnings, the Tribunal had taken only an amount of 8,000/- for Subhakumar vs Joy on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131604158/
2
a period of two months, which is on the lower side.
The claimant sustained total amputation of left little finger and left ring finger.

Considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the claimant, I find it appropriate to take a 2026:KER:11188 M.A.C.A. NO. 2184 OF 2014 period of three months for awarding compensation towards loss of earnings.
Since the monthly income is refixed at 6,500/-, the total compensation payable under the head is recalculated as: 19,500/- (6500 x 3).
The Tribunal has only awarded an amount of 8,000/- under the said head.
Thus, there will be an additional amount of 11,500/- under the head loss of income.
Compensation for reduction of amenities in life:- The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the Tribunal has granted an amount of 5,000/- under the said head.

Considering the loss of enjoyment in life, I am inclined to grant 30,000/-
towards loss of amenities.

Thus, there will be an additional amount of 25,000/-
under the head loss of amenities.

Compensation for permanent disability :- The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the Tribunal had taken only 5% disability even though there was amputation of left little finger and left ring finger.
Even going by the Workmen's Compensation Act, for amputation of loss of two fingers of one hand, the percentage of loss of earning capacity is taken as 20%.

Considering the age of the appellant being 40 years, and the injuries sustained, I find 2026:KER:11188 M.A.C.A. NO. 2184 OF 2014 it appropriate to refix the percentage of functional disability as 20%.

Since the monthly income of the appellant is refixed at 6,500/- the compensation payable under the head permanent disability is recalculated thus: 2,34,000/- (6500 x 12x 15 x 20/100) as the total compensation payable.
Since, the Tribunal has awarded an amount of 36,000/-, there will be an additional amount of 1,98,000/- under the head permanent disability.

6. Though the appellant claimed enhancement of compensation under the other heads, on a perusal of the records available, I am not inclined to interfere with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads since it appears to be just and reasonable.
Since the appeal is of the year 2014, I find it appropriate to fix the interest @ 6% per annum on the enhanced amount.

7. On a perusal of the impugned award, it is seen that the tribunal awarded penal interest at the rate of 9%, which is not legally sustainable in view of the judgment of the apex court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Keshav Bahadur [2004 (2) SCC 370].

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Keshav Bahadur [2004 (2) SCC 370]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the direction of the tribunal awarding penal interest @ 9% per annum is hereby set aside.

Thus, the impugned award of the Tribunal is modified as follows:-
Sl.

3
by the Tribunal appeal compensatio 1 Compensation for loss 8,000 11,500 19,50  of income 2

Compensation for 2,600 Nil 2,600  bystander's expense 3 Compensation for 2,000 Nil 2,000  transport to hospital 4 Extra nourishment 1,000 Nil 1,00 5 Compensation for pain 12,000 18,000 30,00  and suffering 6 Compensation for 67,000 Nil 67,00  medical expense 7 Compensation for 36,000 1,98,000 2,34,000  permanent disability 8 Compensation for 5,000 25,000 30,00  reduction in amenities  in life  TOTAL 1,33,600 2,52,500 3,86,100  rounded as  1,34,000

Accordingly, the appeal is allowed in part and  appellant/claimant is awarded an additional compensation of 2,52,500/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Fifty Two Thousand Five Hundred only) over and above the compensation awarded by the Tribunal with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization and proportionate costs against the first respondent being the owner.

The 1st respondent shall deposit the said amount together with interest and costs within a 2026:KER:11188 M.A.C.A. NO. 2184 OF 2014 period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
The direction of the tribunal awarding penal interest @ 9% per annum is hereby set aside.

The appellant/claimant shall furnish copies of the PAN Card, ADHAAR Card and bank details before the tribunal within a period of one month so as to enable the 1st respondent to make the deposit as ordered above.
In case of failure to furnish details as above, it shall be open for the 1st respondent to deposit the said amount before the Tribunal.
Upon such deposit being made, the entire amount shall be disbursed to the appellant at the earliest in accordance with law.
However, it is made clear that the enhanced compensation will not carry interest for the period of delay of 448 days in filing the appeal.
